newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index ends at a 2-mth low.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index ends at a 2-mth low.

text.p: Lingering concerns on the peso and PLDT's fall in New York sent Manila shares reeling on Thursday, causing the index to hit a two-month low at close, traders said.
The main index settled lower for the fourth consecutive day, closing 78.05 points down, or 3.01 percent, at 2,511.15.

"Overnight rates went up again as the speculative attacks on the peso seem to be active. Also PLDT's lower close in New York did not help the market any," said David de la Cruz, Amsteel Securities vice-president for marketing.
The Central Bank raised its overnight borrowing rate by two percentage points to 32 percent on Thursday. on Wednesday on profit-taking, traders said.
PLDT closed 40 pesos lower at 850 pesos after recovering from an intra-day low of 815 pesos.
Turnover was slightly higher at 2.5 billion pesos against 2.2 billion the previous day. Losers outpaced gainers 105 to 25 with 50 issues unchanged.
Except for the oil sector, all the sub-indices fell. The fall was led by the banking and financial sector.

"If the dealing volume at the Philippine Dealing System is lower, then we may see a brighter tommorrow for the equities market. If not, it will be bleak," said Bing Trinidad, sales manager at DBS Securities.
